newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S POSTABANK SECURITIES RATES BCHEM AS 'BUY'.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S POSTABANK SECURITIES RATES BCHEM AS 'BUY'.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem are undervalued compared to the rest of the market, Hungary's Postabank Securities said, rating the stocks as 'buy.'

"Shares are traded at a 1997 P/E of six times at present (with March 12 closing price of 6,150 forints) which is approximately a 40 percent discount to the market," analyst Ferenc Szollosi said in a company report.
"We believe that the discount should decrease and therefore recommend the purchase of shares," he said.
Szollosi said that company's risk is decreasing gradually as a result of product diversification, good cost management and a strong financial position.

Borsodchem produces PVC and is the only manufacturer of methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) in central and eastern Europe. In addition, Austria's Krems Chemie AG plans to build a formaldehyde plant in Hungary, jointly with Borsodchem.
Last year Borsodchem boosted its PVC capacity to an annual 250 kilotonnes from 210 kilotonnes and its MDI capacity to 32.5 kilotonnes from 25 kilotoness.
"We estimate that the new capacity will result in approximately a seven to 7.5 billion forint increase in sales," Szollosi said.
He added that he expected Borsodchem's sales to rise 26 percent this year to 55.4 billion forints, and saw the company's earnings per share ratio rising 50 percent to 1,025 forints in 1997.
